text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Dutch securities trade watchdog STE decides to stop publishing information about share ownership in bourse-listed companies. (p1)
- Civil service pension fund ABP withdraws subscription for shares in temporary employment agency Vedior after flotation price is raised to 37-40 guilders from 33-37. (p1)
- Maritime services company Smit Internationale halts plans to return vessels to Dutch shipping register because of "absurd" wage demands from seamen's union. (p1)
- Cost of healthcare in the Netherlands rose 2.7 pct in 1996 to 57.6 billion guilders. (p5)
- Finance ministry starts publishing an issue calendar for Dutch Treasury Certificates. (p17)
- Party conference selects Health Minister Els Borst to head centre left D66 party's list of candidates in next year's parliamentary election. (p1)
- Prime Minister Wim Kok will not allow journalists to travel with him on his tour of European capitals to prepare for the EU's Amsterdam summit meeting on June 16 and 17. (p3)
- Many vets believe government measures to combat the country's swine fever epidemic are ineffective. (p3)
- Chief executive of Rotterdam port calls for creation of a national holding company which would run all Dutch seaports as subsidiaries. (p11)
